cards.power: The BBC-Smasher. Invades red cells and makes them Sticky, jamming brain and kidney pipes.
cards.lore: The deadliest clan. Uses Sequestration to hide from the Spleen-Sentry.
cards.gradeReason: BBC-Smasher jamming brain and kidney pipes — immediate villain embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gritty medical horror comic. Subject: spiked parasite bursting from red blood cell. Mood: lethal and inevitable.

cards.power: The Sleeper-Cell. Hides in the Liver-Basement for months or years.
cards.lore: Requires Primaquine-the-Purger to clear. Watch out for G6PD-deficient beasts—the purger will melt their blood!
cards.gradeReason: Sleeper-Cell hiding in liver basement for years — haunting stealth villain role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir shadow watercolor. Subject: hooded figure lurking in basement shadows clutching stopwatch. Mood: patient and sinister.

cards.power: The Parasite-Pulse. Strikes during the most active stage, clearing blood-Load instantly.
cards.lore: Derived from Sweet Wormwood. The Heavy-Artillery for Falci.
cards.gradeReason: Heavy-Artillery framing is great but drug card needs setup to embody cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic epic watercolor. Subject: armored warrior swinging glowing hammer through infected blood cells. Mood: decisive and powerful.

cards.power: The Old-School-Zap. Ancient guardian, but toxic and Bitter to the host.
cards.lore: Triggers Insulin-the-Enforcer, crashing the host's sugar-stats.
cards.gradeReason: Old-School-Zap is evocative but toxicity side-effect framing requires explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage apothecary illustration. Subject: ancient crumbling warrior firing electric bolt while clutching ears. Mood: powerful but self-destructive.

cards.power: The Massive-Drain. Opens gut Chloride-Gates, flushing body water in a single tide.
cards.lore: Secretes Cholera Toxin. ORS-the-Refiller is needed more than antibiotics to survive the flood.
cards.gradeReason: Massive-Drain flushing body water in single tide — instantly embodiable flood villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action watercolor comic. Subject: walrus-creature blasting open fire hydrant flooding gut corridor. Mood: overwhelming and chaotic.

cards.power: The Trojan-Horse. Hitches a ride inside Nacro-Maggie cleaners to invade bone marrow.
cards.lore: Spreads via the Gallbladder-Garrlaoa. Carriers spread the infection without feeling a punch.
cards.gradeReason: Trojan-Horse sneaking inside macrophages to invade bone marrow — perfect stealth role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medieval siege comic. Subject: armored villain riding mechanical wooden horse through castle gate. Mood: cunning and hidden.

cards.power: The Suction-Stall. Uses a Suction-Disk to stick to the gut wall, blocking fat absorption.
cards.lore: Backpacker's Bane. Cysts are armor-plated against chlorine.
cards.gradeReason: Suction-Stall is a fun move but fat-blocking is described more than performed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gross-out biology watercolor. Subject: blob creature with giant suction cups plastered to pink intestinal wall. Mood: stubborn and sticky.

cards.power: The Organ-Scarrer. Eggs trigger a massive Fibro-Fiona riot, turning liver/bladder to stone.
cards.lore: Lives in venous plexus. Salamsr's Itch is the first sign of invasion.
cards.gradeReason: Turning liver and bladder to stone — visceral, immediate monster-king embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark fantasy watercolor. Subject: crowned snail lord on throne with stone-textured liver looming behind. Mood: regal and destructive.

cards.power: The Capillary-Crasher. Melts Endothelial-Armor, causing systemic leakage and collapse.
cards.lore: Paralyzes Dendritic-Directors early, allowing a lethal Cytokine-Storm to finish the host.
cards.gradeReason: Capillary-Crasher melting armor and causing total collapse — peak villain embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: apocalyptic horror watercolor. Subject: red serpentine virus bursting through blood vessel walls. Mood: unstoppable and catastrophic.

cards.power: The Joint-Crush. Makes every bone feel like it's snapping.
cards.lore: Antibody-Enhancement makes a second match with a new strain far deadlier (DHF-the-Hemorrhage).
cards.gradeReason: Joint-Crush making every bone snap — immediate, visceral, no context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: kinetic action watercolor. Subject: raccoon wrestler shattering skeleton opponents with glowing fists. Mood: brutal and explosive.

cards.power: The Ear-Thief. A systemic fever that specifically targets acoustic nerves.
cards.lore: Ribavirin is the only Chemical-Counter if used before the timer runs out.
cards.gradeReason: Ear-Thief is a distinctive hook but targeting acoustic nerves needs framing to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark thriller watercolor. Subject: monstrous rat in burning ruins trailing smoke labeled Silence. Mood: feverish and deafening.

cards.power: The Liver-Executioner. Turns skin gold and vomit black while destroying the Liver-Factory.
cards.lore: Leaves Councilman Bodies in the liver. 17D-Shield vaccine grants a lifetime of protection.
cards.gradeReason: Skin gold, vomit black, Liver-Executioner — cinematic, immediate, unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: golden horror watercolor. Subject: golden wolf-creature vomiting black torrents under blazing sun. Mood: dramatic and lethal.

cards.power: The Pipe-Obstructer. Grows massive to physically block Bowel-Tunnels or Bile-Ducts.
cards.lore: Takes a Grand-Tour of the body, traveling from gut to lungs (Loeffler-the-Cough) and back.
cards.gradeReason: Grand-Tour parasite growing to block pipes — vivid journey villain, immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: body horror anatomical comic. Subject: massive pale worm coiling through intestine corridors blocking all passages. Mood: relentless and invasive.

cards.power: The Blood-Sucker. Bites into Intestinal-Wallpaper to drink blood drop by drop.
cards.lore: Causes the Grey-Faint—the host goes pale as all Iron-Tokens are drained.
cards.gradeReason: Blood-Sucker drinking drop by drop until Grey-Faint — pure vampire embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic watercolor. Subject: fanged goblin biting pink intestinal wall drawing blood streams. Mood: predatory and draining.

cards.power: The Fluid-Dam. Clogs Lymph-Drains, mutating limbs into heavy, skin-thickened pillars.
cards.lore: Worms-in-the-Wires stay for years. Requires DEC-the-Worm-Riller.
cards.gradeReason: Fluid-Dam and pillar-limbs are vivid but DEC treatment note clutters the persona.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grotesque body horror watercolor. Subject: swollen creature with pillar-thick legs struggling under own weight. Mood: tragic and heavy.

cards.power: The Sight-Stealer. Triggers intense Skin-Itch and slowly calcifies eyes into Scar-Stone.
cards.lore: Ivermectin-the-Legend is required to stop the Micro-Worm-Migration.
cards.gradeReason: Calcifying eyes into Scar-Stone — harrowing, immediately embodiable villain arc.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tropical horror watercolor. Subject: blackfly dropping microfilariae into troll's clouding eyes beside a river. Mood: slow and inevitable.

cards.power: The Spread-Velocity. Tells the team how many new infections one Source will create.
cards.lore: R0 < 1 means the outbreak dies. R0 > 1 means the Pathogen-Fire spreads.
cards.gradeReason: Spread-Velocity is a great concept card but epidemiological mechanic needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dynamic infographic watercolor. Subject: single lit match igniting field of matches in exponential chain reaction. Mood: mathematical and alarming.

cards.power: The Pathogen-Blocker. With enough Vaccine-Shields, the enemy finds no path to the vulnerable.
cards.lore: Protects the Immune-Naive by surrounding them with Biological-Armor.
cards.gradeReason: Pathogen-Blocker is clear but systems concept card limits direct performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic group watercolor. Subject: ring of armored animals forming shield wall around unarmored creature. Mood: protective and collective.

cards.power: The Shadow-Hunter. Tracks Pathogen-Footprints to find everyone the enemy has touched.
cards.lore: Crucial for Ebola/Smallpox. Find the Next-Victim before the next fire starts.
cards.gradeReason: Shadow-Hunter tracking footprints in a race — immediate detective roleplay, no context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir detective watercolor. Subject: hound detective following glowing biohazard footprints across a floor map. Mood: urgent and focused.

cards.power: The Arena-Lockdown. Prevents the Infected from entering the ring until the Incubation-Timer clears.
cards.lore: The ultimate Passive-Defense that breaks the transmission chain by force.
cards.gradeReason: Arena-Lockdown is vivid framing but institutional mechanism is not a direct performer role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grim bureaucratic watercolor. Subject: large bear arms crossed blocking arena entrance behind yellow hazard tape. Mood: implacable and containment-focused.

cards.power: The Urban-Smuggler. Loves City-Water and targets hosts inside their own homes.
cards.lore: Extremely high Vector-Competence. The premier delivery truck for the Flavivirus clan.
cards.gradeReason: Urban-Smuggler hiding in city water targeting homes — perfect stealth city villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: urban action watercolor. Subject: striped mosquito in city carrying virus canisters through apartment window. Mood: stealthy and relentless.

cards.power: The Brain-Sleep-Curse. Injects a parasite that crosses the brain barrier, forcing a terminal coma.
cards.lore: Attacks the CNS. The victim becomes lethargic and Dezes-te-Death without a counter-strike.
cards.gradeReason: Brain-Sleep-Curse forcing terminal coma — immediately haunting, embodiable dark curse.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychedelic horror watercolor. Subject: massive metallic fly injecting dark spiral into sleeping armored badger. Mood: trance-like and lethal.

cards.power: The Slow-Lyme-Lock. Hitches a ride to slowly inject a Multi-System-Saboteur.
cards.lore: If not caught early, the Heart-Wires and Joint-Gears begin to fail.
cards.gradeReason: Slow-Lyme-Lock is distinctive but multi-system sabotage needs context to embody cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk watercolor. Subject: mechanical tick clinging to deer flank injecting gears into heart circuit. Mood: slow and insidious.

cards.power: The Skin-Diver. Releases thousands of Torpedo-Worms into the water, waiting for bare skin.
cards.lore: Avoid the Snail-Waters. It's a purely Environmental-Ambush.
cards.gradeReason: Torpedo-Worms ambush in snail-waters — weaponized snail villain is perfectly immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: underwater action watercolor. Subject: steampunk snail submarine launching glowing torpedo larvae at swimmer. Mood: explosive and aquatic.

cards.power: The Anaerobe-Annihilator. Melts Giardi and Amoeba by shredding their DNA.
cards.lore: The Metal-Taste warrior. Never mix with Al-the-Alcohol or the host will vomit endlessly.
cards.gradeReason: Anaerobe-Annihilator shredding DNA with metal-taste — vivid hero identity, instantly playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sci-fi action watercolor. Subject: rhino mech warrior firing green laser that dissolves amoeba monsters. Mood: precise and annihilating.

cards.power: The Spasm-Strike. Triggers a Massive-Cramp causing all worms to lose their grip.
cards.lore: The Universal-Fluke-Fighter. The only eviction notice Schisto-the-Snail-Lord respects.
cards.gradeReason: Spasm-Strike making worms lose grip — the universal eviction notice is immediate and satisfying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fantasy wizard watercolor. Subject: lightning-staffed mage sending electrical cramp through mass of writhing worms. Mood: decisive and liberating.

cards.power: The Micro-Nerve-Gas. Paralyzes the nerves of Oncho and Sarcoptes-the-Itch-Mite.
cards.lore: A Mass-Drug-Administration hero capable of clearing entire villages of Parasite-Punks.
cards.gradeReason: Nobel Prize hero clearing entire villages of Parasite-Punks — legendary status, immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic epic watercolor. Subject: golden eagle warrior swooping over village scattering parasite creatures into dust. Mood: triumphant and sweeping.

cards.power: The Starvation-Strike. Steps worms from Eating-Glucose, starving them to death inside the host.
cards.lore: Broad-Spectrum-Worm-Warrior covering Ascaris, Hookworm, and Pinworm.
cards.gradeReason: Starvation-Strike is clever but pharmaceutical mechanism card needs more persona to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial action watercolor. Subject: bulldog bouncer locking glucose kitchen door while worms starve outside. Mood: systematic and final.

cards.power: The Global-Alert. Issues the Warning-Siren coordinating all Arena-Responders.
cards.lore: Provides the ultimate Rules-of-Engagement during a Pandemic-Panic.
cards.gradeReason: Global-Alert conducting all Arena-Responders — immediate conductor/commander role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: epic orchestral watercolor. Subject: owl on conductor podium directing animal health worker orchestra under crisis lights. Mood: urgent and authoritative.

cards.power: The Shield-Preserver. Prevents Vaccine-Shields from melting into useless Water-Tokens.
cards.lore: The hardest part of a Tropical-Match is getting shields to Remote-Rings without them getting warm.
cards.gradeReason: Infrastructure concept card — no character to embody, purely logistics mechanism description.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial landscape watercolor. Subject: ice-armored tank convoy crossing desert with frozen vaccine cargo glowing. Mood: tense and precarious.

cards.power: The Primary-Barrier. Stops Choler and Typhi before they even reach the arena.
cards.lore: Clean water is recognised as the single most powerful Antibiotic ever discovered.
cards.gradeReason: Primary-Barrier blocking enemies before they enter — builder-defender, immediately playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic construction watercolor. Subject: beaver construction worker building brick wall with clean water flowing beside it. Mood: steadfast and foundational.

cards.power: The Night-Guard. Blocks the Anopheles-Assassins from attacking sleepers.
cards.lore: The simplest, cheapest, and most effective way to drop the Malaria-Score in any village.
cards.gradeReason: Night-Guard blocking Anopheles-Assassins — immediate, simple, heroic guardian role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: glowing night defense watercolor. Subject: blue mesh dome protecting sleeping dog from mosquito army. Mood: safe and vigilant.

cards.power: The Volcanic-Ulcer. Creates a Crater-Lump that refuses to heal, leaving a Victory-Scar.
cards.lore: If it evolves to Visceral-Leish, it targets the Spleen-and-Liver-Base—100% lethal.
cards.gradeReason: Volcanic-Ulcer refusing to heal with 100% lethal visceral upgrade — vivid escalating villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: volcanic horror watercolor. Subject: erupting crater wound on skin with sandfly perched triumphantly above. Mood: festering and escalating.

cards.power: The Numb-Invader. Kills Sensation-Nerves, hiding the pain of Arena-Trauma (burns/cuts).
cards.lore: A Social-Stigma-Weapon. Without treatment, secondary Scuff-Matches cost the host fingers and toes.
cards.gradeReason: Numb-Invader hiding pain is clever but historical stigma framing adds complexity to embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: aged medieval watercolor. Subject: spotted badger ringing bell by torchlight with nerve endings visibly fading. Mood: ancient and isolating.

cards.power: The Blueprint-Hacker. Breaches the Uterine-Fortress to sabotage fetal brain development.
cards.lore: A mild fever for the adult, but inflicts a devastating Permanent-GCS-Debuff on the next generation.
cards.gradeReason: Blueprint-Hacker sabotaging the next generation — sinister generational villain, instantly clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cyberpunk horror watercolor. Subject: dark virus entity hacking holographic brain blueprint inside a fortress. Mood: covert and devastating.

cards.power: The Living-Anchor. A fly lays an egg on a mesquite, which delivers the Worm-Guest directly into the skin.
cards.lore: You can literally feel it Wiggle. The only way out is to Smother-the-Breathing-Hole.
cards.gradeReason: You can literally feel it wiggle — most viscerally immediate card in the deck, G1 guaranteed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gross-out nature horror watercolor. Subject: botfly larva with tiny periscope emerging from inflamed skin wound. Mood: squirm-inducing and alive.

cards.power: The Water-Panic. Terrifies the host of drinking, sparking a Foaming-Rage.
cards.lore: Climbs the Nerve-Cables to the brain. Post-Exposure-Shield must be deployed Immediately!
cards.gradeReason: Water-Panic and Foaming-Rage — 100% lethal with immediate feral embodiment, no context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: feral horror watercolor. Subject: rabid werewolf cowering from water glass with foam at mouth and glowing red eyes. Mood: frenzied and terminal.

cards.power: The Wave-Attack. Fever strikes in rolling Waves, giving false hope before crushing the host again.
cards.lore: Hides in the Reticuloendothelial-Vaults. Requires a Double-Antibiotic-Strike for weeks.
cards.gradeReason: Wave-Attack with false-hope rhythm is distinctive but undulant pattern needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wave horror watercolor. Subject: figure on raft repeatedly engulfed by rolling red fever waves then briefly surfacing. Mood: cyclical and exhausting.

cards.power: The Yellow-Kidney-Strike. Invades through skin cuts during floods to trash the liver and kidneys.
cards.lore: Mimics Dengue/Malaria. The giveaway is Conjuactival-Suffusion (Red eyes with zero pus).
cards.gradeReason: Yellow-Kidney-Strike flooding through skin cuts — immediate disaster-zone villain with signature tell.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: disaster horror watercolor. Subject: yellow mutant dog wading flooded streets attacking glowing kidney organs. Mood: contaminating and opportunistic.

cards.power: The Black-Eschar. Creates a Painless-Black-Crater outside, but operates as a Silent-Killer inside the lungs.
cards.lore: The Spore-Shield lets him survive in dirt for decades, waiting patiently for a new victim.
cards.gradeReason: Painless black crater hiding lung killer + decades of patience — haunting stealth assassin.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial gothic watercolor. Subject: black spore explosion eye with factory smoke and painless black crater on skin. Mood: patient and inevitable.

cards.power: The Tissue-Melter. Uses Proteases to melt the gut wall and swim to the liver to build a Pus-Nest.
cards.lore: If he reaches the Liver-Basement, the host suffers high fever and a severe Right-Sided-Ache.
cards.gradeReason: Melting gut wall to swim to liver and build Pus-Nest — immediate, disgusting, embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gross body horror watercolor. Subject: slime ghost creature melting through intestinal wall leaving pus trail towards liver. Mood: relentless and festering.

cards.power: The Endless-Loop. Reproduces endlessly inside the host, never needing the outside world.
cards.lore: Predni-the-Systemic-Steroid sends Strongy into Hyper-Drive, flooding the body and ending the match.
cards.gradeReason: Endless-Loop never needing the outside world — perfect self-contained monster identity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: infinite horror watercolor. Subject: snake worm eating its own tail in spiral multiplying within human silhouette. Mood: self-perpetuating and dizzying.

cards.power: The Acid-Shield-Breaker. Venta a Cloud-of-Ammonia to survive stomach acid while burning the Wallpaper.
cards.lore: Master of the Slow-Burn, occupying Antrum-Alley for decades.
cards.gradeReason: Venting ammonia cloud to survive acid while burning the wallpaper for decades — slow arsonist villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: urban decay watercolor. Subject: hazmat figure spraying green ammonia cloud while setting stomach lining walls on fire. Mood: chronic and corrosive.

cards.power: The Arena-Clearer. Spreads so fast it knocks out entire Wrestling-Cruise-Ships in 24 hours.
cards.lore: The Winter Vomiting Bug. Zero immunity—Noro can hit you over and over again.
cards.gradeReason: Knocking out an entire cruise ship in 24 hours with zero immunity — perfectly chaotic villain.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: disaster comedy-horror watercolor. Subject: green goblin vomiting biohazard cloud across luxury cruise ship deck. Mood: explosive and unstoppable.

cards.power: The Parasite-Counter. Thick smear finds the enemy; Thin smear identifies their Clan.
cards.lore: The absolute Gold-Standard for confirming Falci-the-Killer.
cards.gradeReason: Gold-Standard naming is perfect but diagnostic tool cards are harder to embody as performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scientific detective watercolor. Subject: magnifying glass over microscope slides revealing glowing parasite army. Mood: forensic and precise.

cards.power: The 15-Minute-Verdict. Gives the Attending-Boss an instant Yes/No in the middle of the jungle.
cards.lore: Doesn't reveal the Blood-Load, but confirms if the enemy is in the ring.
cards.gradeReason: 15-Minute-Verdict is great framing but diagnostic tool needs more performer cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: field medicine watercolor. Subject: glowing rapid test strip showing red lines on blood-spattered jungle backdrop. Mood: urgent and decisive.

cards.power: The Brain-Secret-Reader. Reveals if Meningitis or Cerebral Malaria is knocking on the Brain-Bunker.
cards.lore: Essential staging tool for the Tsetse-Sleep-Fly curse.
cards.gradeReason: Brain-Secret-Reader is evocative but needle procedure card is descriptive rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mystical medicine watercolor. Subject: glowing needle extracting crystal-clear CSF from spine while brain glows overhead. Mood: precise and revealing.

cards.power: The History-Reader. Tells the team if the host is fighting now, or if they won the match years ago.
cards.lore: Uses Enzyme-Linkage to illuminate historical Pathogen-Footprints.
cards.gradeReason: History-Reader distinguishing IgM/IgG is clever but laboratory mechanism limits performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: historical detective watercolor. Subject: robotic archivist holding glowing antibody jar illuminating ancient battle records. Mood: scholarly and revelatory.

cards.power: The Shield-Distributor. Ensures even the Poorest-Arenas get the Vaccine-Shields they desperately need.
cards.lore: The Economic-Shield. Without GAVI, Measles and Polio would win the match every single time.
cards.gradeReason: Shield-Distributor is a great role but organizational scale makes direct embodiment indirect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: divine epic watercolor. Subject: divine lion raining glowing vaccine shields down on poor arenas below. Mood: benevolent and global.

cards.power: The Early-Warning-System. Scans for the first sign of a Fever-Cluster to abort a Pandemic-Panic.
cards.lore: Information is Power. Catches the fire when it's still just a spark.
cards.gradeReason: Catching the fire when it's just a spark — sentinel role is immediate and heroic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: radar thriller watercolor. Subject: giant dish antenna scanning glowing world map detecting tiny red fever dot. Mood: vigilant and anticipatory.

cards.power: The Total-Arena-Vision. Recognizes you can't protect the wrestler without protecting the Environment-Arena and Animal-Allies.
cards.lore: 75% of new Infection-Assassins originate from the animal kingdom.
cards.gradeReason: Paradigm card — describes a philosophy, offers no immediate performer identity or action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ecological epic watercolor. Subject: lion, cow, and forest in swirling interconnected energy spiral. Mood: holistic and interconnected.

cards.power: The Perfect-Storm. When hosts are forced into crowded Tented-Arenas without clean water, pathogens feast.
cards.lore: The ultimate, heartbreaking challenge for Global-Outbreak-Defenders.
cards.gradeReason: Situation card — important sobering content but purely descriptive, no role to inhabit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: somber humanitarian watercolor. Subject: grey tent camp in rain with danger sign and distant pathogens circling. Mood: sobering and urgent.

cards.power: The Outbreak-Orchestrator. Synthesizes the clues to break the chain.
cards.lore: Think global, act local. Is it the vector, the water, or the contact? Find the source or the arena falls! Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Outbreak-Orchestrator asking the right questions — FrizzleBob as playable hero is instant G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: explorer hero watercolor. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit in safari hat with magnifying glass, globe and question marks. Mood: curious and commanding.

cards.cardName: Synthesis Quest 1 — The Fever of the Forest
cards.power: Identify the Liver-Executioner (Yellow-the-Jaundice-Jack) and name the Urban-Smuggler (Aedes-the-Tiger).
cards.lore: A wrestler returns from the Amazon with a high fever, black vomit, and yellow skin. He didn't have his 17D-Shield.
cards.gradeReason: Clinical case scenario — educational challenge card, requires knowledge not immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: jungle mystery watercolor. Subject: sick wrestler with yellow skin surrounded by Amazon vines and question marks. Mood: diagnostic and tense.

cards.power: Identify the RBC-Smasher (Falci-the-Killer) and choose the Hammer-Weapon (Artesu-the-Hammer).
cards.lore: A pup in a malaria-zone is unconscious and having seizures. The Thick-Smear is full of Sticky-RBC-Shards.
cards.gradeReason: Clinical scenario with treatment decision — educational challenge, not a performance cue.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: urgent medical watercolor. Subject: lightning shattering brain with red sticky blood cell shards and question marks. Mood: seizure-urgent and diagnostic.

cards.power: Identify the Snail-Lord (Schisto-the-Snail-Lord) and apply the Worm-Paralyzer (Prazi-the-Spasm-Strike).
cards.lore: A wrestler who swam in a freshwater lake has an enlarged liver and Portal-Gears that are turning to stone.
cards.gradeReason: Clinical reasoning scenario — well-designed case but descriptive educational challenge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: freshwater horror watercolor. Subject: stone question mark in green lake water with snails circling and stone liver behind. Mood: cryptic and aquatic.

verdict: FrizzleBob's most medically complete deck yet — 56 pathogens, vectors, drugs, diagnostics, and systems cards locked into a single coherent tropical medicine universe, with cross-references firing between cards (Snail-Lord respects only Prazi's eviction notice; Oncho falls to Iver-the-Legend). The naming architecture — Pathogen-the-Effect — is the strongest in the MedKayfab library, yielding G1 rates above 58%. Three G3 cards (Cold-Chain, One-Health-Paradigm, Refugee-Camp-Crisis) are structurally important but refuse to put on a costume — candidates for redesign as arena condition cards. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: From Falci-the-Killer jamming your brain pipes to Noro clearing an entire cruise ship in 24 hours — this 56-card deck turns tropical medicine into a combat sport you'll never forget.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: TROPICAL MEDICINE – Global Outbreak & The Vector Vengeance (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the malaria that hides in the liver and kills through the brain, the waterborne bugs that empty a body in a day, and the worms, vectors and antiparasitic drugs the boards keep abstract.

It is day nine since the flight home and the fever has come back. Your patient went trekking, came back tired, shook it off, and now sits in front of you burning at forty with a headache that started this morning. Somewhere in their red cells, Falci is already gluing them to the walls of the brain and the kidney, sequestering where no blood film thinks to look. You have hours, not days. And the one question that decides everything is the one a tired traveller never volunteers: where exactly did you go, and did anything bite you.

MedKayfab Global Outbreak turns the returning-traveller workup and the outbreak ward into a narrative wrestling match, every pathogen, vector and drug a fighter with a tell. Stop memorizing tropical disease as a regional checklist. Start performing the outbreak before it performs on you.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (15pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like FALCI-THE-KILLER, Noro-the-Cruise-Ship-Chaos, and Rabies-the-Hydrophobe
- Three Synthesis Quest cards that hand you a fever and dare you to walk it back to the named fighters
- Free lifetime updates as guidelines evolve

What's in the deck
This deck gives a face to the bugs, the bites, the drugs and the systems that carry them. You'll meet FALCI-THE-KILLER, deadliest of the malaria clan, who sticks infected red cells to the brain and kidney pipes and hides from the Spleen-Sentry by sequestering where no blood film can catch it. You'll meet Noro-the-Cruise-Ship-Chaos, who clears an entire ship in twenty-four hours on a dose of a few dozen viral particles. And you'll meet Rabies-the-Hydrophobe, the one fighter you never want across the table, because once it shows its face the match is already lost. The roster keeps firing cross-references at itself: the Snail-Lord of schistosomiasis answers only to Prazi's eviction notice, and River-Blindness goes down to Iver-the-Legend.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor: the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (vector, reservoir, drug), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the field challenge). Mechanism Flash is the brutal mode: name the vector, the killer step and the drug in one breath without looking, or the traveller on the Stage never makes the connecting flight. The three Synthesis Quest cards close the loop, handing you an undifferentiated fever and making you trace it back through the fighters you already met.

Honest cognitive load
This is a wide deck, not a deep one. It sweeps the whole tropical map, pathogens, vectors, antiparasitic drugs, diagnostics and the health systems that contain an outbreak, which makes it a strong survey for medical students, residents heading into infectious disease, travel or tropical medicine, and anyone working in global health. It pairs naturally with Microbiology and Infectiology for the bug-level detail under each character, and with Emergency Medicine for the night the returning-traveller fever crashes before the diagnosis lands.
